Longwave radiation emitted by the surface

Source: R/metric-radiation.R
ef_rl_out.Rd

Computes the longwave radiation emitted by the land surface, \(R_{L\uparrow}\), from its temperature and broadband emissivity. The result is the rl_out argument of ef_net_radiation() and does not include the reflected incoming longwave radiation, which ef_net_radiation() accounts for separately.

Usage

ef_rl_out(lst, emissivity)

Arguments

lst

Numeric. Land surface temperature \(T_s\) [K], > 0 (e.g. MODIS LST with scale factor and quality control applied).

emissivity

Numeric. Broadband surface emissivity \(\varepsilon_0\) [-], in (0, 1]. It must be the same emissivity later passed to ef_net_radiation().

Value

A numeric vector of \(R_{L\uparrow}\) [W m-2] with the common length and dim of the inputs.

Details

$$R_{L\uparrow} = \varepsilon_0 \sigma T_s^4$$ with \(\sigma\) the Stefan-Boltzmann constant (CODATA 2018 exact value, decision RC-07). With the rounded 5.67e-8 W m-2 K-4 of some METRIC implementations the result differs by about 6.6e-5 in relative terms.

Consistency of the emissivity (decision RC-14, open): the broadband emissivity should be consistent with the narrow-band emissivities assumed by the LST retrieval; the same value must be used here and in ef_net_radiation() (otherwise a spurious longwave term appears). A radiometer measurement of the upwelling longwave radiation (emitted plus reflected) is not interchangeable with this output.

Assumptions: grey-body surface with broadband emissivity; lst represents the radiating surface of the whole pixel; instantaneous value.

Arguments must be numeric and have length 1 or a common length; matrix or array arguments must share their dim. A non-positive or infinite lst, or an emissivity outside (0, 1], raises earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error). Plausibility of lst (e.g. values in degrees Celsius by mistake) needs a threshold without a documented reference and is not checked. Missing values (e.g. cloudy MODIS pixels) propagate.

Verification status

CANDIDATA (corroborated): the form \(\varepsilon_0 \sigma T_s^4\) is the one used by the water package (v1.0) and by an independent secondary source (Wasti, 2020) together with the net radiation of ef_net_radiation(); contrast with Allen et al. (2007) is pending.

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

See also

Other radiation functions: ef_atm_emissivity(), ef_net_radiation(), ef_rl_in(), ef_rs_in(), ef_solar_geometry(), ef_tau_sw()

Examples

# Surface at 300 K with emissivity 0.98
ef_rl_out(lst = 300, emissivity = 0.98)
#> [1] 450.1143

# Matrix input keeps its dim
ef_rl_out(lst = matrix(c(295, 300, 305, 310), 2), emissivity = 0.97)
#>          [,1]     [,2]
#> [1,] 416.5542 475.9736
#> [2,] 445.5213 507.9609
